raw_response:
I’m 54 this year, and I’ve farmed this land a long time. I don’t change too much unless I see a reason. Wheat and maize are still my main crops because that’s the steady way here, and I have a well so I can keep them alive in a dry spell. But with only 2 people at home and some off-farm work, I can’t spread myself too thin. Cotton takes more picking and more watching, so I’ll keep only a small piece in cotton and put most land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. Last year the input prices were not low, so I won’t push fertilizer too hard, but I also don’t dare use too little because if wheat or maize gets weak, the loss is bigger than saving a little cash. I’ll do mostly what people around me do: wheat gets base fertilizer plus one topdressing, maize gets a simpler plan right after wheat harvest, and cotton I manage lighter because of labor. If rain is decent, I save one irrigation; if it stays dry, I use the well at the key times.
